claims.title: Supplier paperwork may be intercepted on the unverified public-to-vendor portal path
claims.description: `flow:entity:supplier>process:supplier-portal>upload-documents` carries supplier staff contact details and compliance paperwork tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, yet its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If transport protection is absent or ineffective, an on-path attacker can intercept uploads between `entity:supplier` and `process:supplier-portal` as they cross into `boundary:vendor-platform`; the supplier's public-internet placement is an inferred endpoint placement, not a confirmed public exposure fact. The disclosed documents can enable targeted social engineering of supplier staff and reveal operational compliance information retained in `store:document-store`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditional on the unknown transport controls: the flow crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to `boundary:vendor-platform`, so a capable path observer needs no portal credential. Impact is medium because the flow carries `pii` and business-critical compliance documents, although the model does not establish corpus scale.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce TLS for supplier uploads
mitigations.detail: Establish the protocol and set `encryption_in_transit` for `flow:entity:supplier>process:supplier-portal>upload-documents` to current TLS; require certificate validation and protect all upload endpoints.

claims.title: Category-manager document reviews may be exposed on an unverified corporate-to-vendor connection
claims.description: `flow:entity:category-manager>process:supplier-portal>review-documents` crosses from `boundary:corporate-network` to `boundary:vendor-platform` while its protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the connection lacks effective transport encryption, an attacker with a position on that route can intercept document reviews, approvals, and rejections, exposing supplier-related `pii` and business-critical review decisions. The information can reveal which suppliers or documents warrant follow-on targeting in `process:supplier-portal` or `store:document-store`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium, conditional on the unknown transport controls, because observing the corporate-to-vendor route requires a network foothold rather than merely reaching a public interface. Impact is medium because the flow is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data` and exposes approval activity.

mitigations.detail: Verify the portal protocol and enforce TLS with current certificate validation for `flow:entity:category-manager>process:supplier-portal>review-documents`; ensure review content is never sent over a downgraded transport path.

claims.title: Uploaded documents may be visible on the portal-to-document-store path
claims.description: `flow:process:supplier-portal>store:document-store>store-documents` carries uploaded compliance documents tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, but its protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If this internal vendor-platform hop is unencrypted, an attacker positioned within or observing the vendor platform can intercept documents before they rest in `store:document-store`. Captured contact information and compliance material can support targeted attacks against suppliers and disclose the contents later reviewed through `process:supplier-portal`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low, conditional on the unknown transport control, because an attacker must first obtain a position inside or able to observe the vendor platform path. Impact is medium because the flow transports `pii` and business-critical compliance documents.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS or an equivalently authenticated encrypted channel for `flow:process:supplier-portal>store:document-store>store-documents`, including service-to-storage traffic inside the vendor platform.

claims.title: The nightly supplier extract may be intercepted between the vendor and landing bucket
claims.description: `flow:entity:portal-vendor>store:landing-bucket>push-nightly-extract` crosses from `boundary:vendor-platform` into `boundary:cloud-account` carrying the nightly supplier data extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`; its protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` remain unknown. If the end-to-end transport claim does not correspond to protected channel encryption, an on-path attacker can intercept the extract in transit. The captured extract then supplies supplier data that is loaded by `process:supplier-master-service` and written into `store:supplier-database`, creating a bulk disclosure beyond the portal session.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium, conditional on the unknown transport controls, because an attacker must observe the vendor-to-cloud boundary-crossing transfer. Impact is high because a nightly supplier data extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data` can expose a bulk dataset and is subsequently propagated into `store:supplier-database`.

mitigations.summary: Use a verifiable encrypted vendor-to-bucket transfer
mitigations.detail: Set and verify TLS or mutually authenticated transfer protection for `flow:entity:portal-vendor>store:landing-bucket>push-nightly-extract`, with certificate validation and a dedicated authenticated vendor delivery identity.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the extract independently of the channel
mitigations.detail: Require the vendor to encrypt the extract before delivery using keys controlled by the cloud-account recipient, so a captured transport artifact is not readable.

claims.title: The supplier master service may receive the landing extract over an unverified internal channel
claims.description: `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract` is a read flow carrying the nightly supplier extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, while its protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If this cloud-account path lacks effective encryption, an attacker able to observe that internal hop can intercept the extract as `process:supplier-master-service` retrieves it. The same data is then used to populate `store:supplier-database`, so one capture can disclose the supplier-record population rather than a single portal interaction.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low, conditional on the unknown transport controls, because the attacker needs an observation point on an internal cloud-account path. Impact is high because the read flow carries the nightly supplier extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data` and feeds the supplier-record database.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS for `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract` and authenticate the bucket endpoint and the service identity.

claims.title: Supplier records may be intercepted while the master service writes the database
claims.description: `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:supplier-database>write-supplier-records` transports supplier records tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, but protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the service-to-database connection is unencrypted, an attacker observing that cloud-account path can intercept records while they are loaded into `store:supplier-database`. The disclosed records can be correlated with the nightly extract and used to target supplier contacts or business operations.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low, conditional on the unknown transport controls, because a path observer must first obtain access within `boundary:cloud-account`. Impact is high because supplier records are tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, and the database represents the loaded record population.

mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:supplier-database>write-supplier-records` to TLS with server certificate validation; use mutual authentication where supported.

claims.title: Vendor-platform document copies may disclose supplier paperwork if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:document-store` retains uploaded compliance documents tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, but both its data classification and `encryption_at_rest` are unknown. If the unresolved at-rest control is absent, an attacker who obtains a storage-layer copy such as media, a snapshot, or an operational export can read the documents without using `process:supplier-portal` or presenting portal credentials. This can disclose supplier staff contact details and compliance material, enabling targeted attacks against the suppliers whose documents are retained there.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_at_rest` value: obtaining an operational copy requires storage-layer access, but such access bypasses the portal path if encryption is absent. Impact is high because the store retains documents tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, potentially across the vendor's document population.

mitigations.summary: Establish and enforce encryption at rest for documents
mitigations.detail: Determine the `encryption_at_rest` posture of `store:document-store`, then require managed encryption covering the primary store and all snapshots, backups, replicas, and exports; restrict key use to necessary vendor operations.

claims.title: A copied landing-bucket extract may reveal supplier data if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:landing-bucket` holds the nightly supplier data extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, yet its data classification and `encryption_at_rest` are unknown. If encryption at rest is not enabled, an attacker holding a copied bucket object, backup, snapshot, or storage media can read the extract directly without authenticating through `process:supplier-master-service`. The extract is subsequently loaded into `store:supplier-database`, so disclosure can expose the supplier data set before its normal processing path.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_at_rest` value because a storage copy bypasses live application controls if the protection is absent. Impact is high because the store contains a nightly supplier extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, which can disclose bulk supplier data.

mitigations.detail: Verify `store:landing-bucket` encryption at rest and enforce managed-key encryption for bucket objects, versioned objects, backups, snapshots, and exports; limit decrypt and export permissions.
Encrypt the delivered extract as an application-level artifact with a recipient-controlled key, so a storage copy remains unreadable without the decryption key.

claims.title: A copied supplier database may disclose supplier records if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:supplier-database` contains loaded supplier records tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, while its data classification and `encryption_at_rest` are unknown. If the unknown at-rest protection resolves to absent encryption, an attacker who obtains a database volume, backup, snapshot, or exported copy can read supplier records without going through `process:supplier-master-service`. The resulting contact and supplier information can be combined with the nightly extract to support broad supplier-targeting campaigns.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_at_rest` value: a copied database artifact bypasses application access controls if storage encryption is absent. Impact is high because the database holds supplier records tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, with potentially broad record scope.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the supplier database and all operational copies
mitigations.detail: Confirm and enforce encryption at rest for `store:supplier-database` using managed keys, explicitly including database backups, snapshots, replicas, and export artifacts; tightly scope key and export access.

claims.title: An over-broad landing-bucket read grant could expose the nightly supplier extract
claims.description: `process:supplier-master-service` reads `store:landing-bucket` through `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract`, which carries the nightly supplier extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`; the flow's authentication is unknown. If the bucket's read authorization is unauthenticated, shared, or broader than this service's required object scope, an attacker using a principal with that access can read the extract directly from `store:landing-bucket`. The disclosure then reaches the data subsequently written into `store:supplier-database` and bypasses the intended batch-processing path.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown authentication and authorization posture of the named read flow: an attacker needs a bucket-reading principal, but the model does not verify that its access is scoped. Impact is high because the read path exposes the nightly extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Restrict bucket reads to a dedicated least-privilege service identity
mitigations.detail: Define and verify authentication on `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract`; deny public and shared access, restrict the service identity to only its required objects and operations, and log bulk or anomalous reads.
